articles.title: Experts slam NIAS report backing Sharavathi project as 'shoddy', question its findings
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Experts have criticised a report by the National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS) for attempting to defend the pumped storage project (PSP) in the Sharavathi Valley Lion-Tailed Macaque Sanctuary by bypassing serious concerns raised by members of statutory bodies and for possible conflicts of interest. The Karnataka Power Corporation Limited has proposed setting up a 2,000 MW power house in the core area of the sanctuary, located in the heart of the Western Ghats. More than 20,000 people opposed the project during the public hearing, while a petition against it on Change.org has garnered more than 50,000 signatures. Last year, a joint committee comprising members of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) and the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) recommended rejecting the project. The committee reviewed the project documents and conducted a site inspection before concluding that the project's large-scale ecological damage was not worth the benefits it promised. Despite its own members' recommendation, the NBWL sought the opinion of NIAS, which brushed aside the joint committee's report and recommended the project. The NIAS report, prepared by Professor R Srikanth, has come to the fore ahead of a meeting on the project convened by the NBWL's Standing Committee on November 27. Experts in the conservation sector and civil society members who reviewed the NIAS report said it failed to address any of the crucial issues raised by the joint committee. Instead, it focused on the generic theme of the need to shift from conventional energy sources to variable renewable energy, portraying PSPs as playing a major role in grid stabilisation. NIAS washing Further, the 'People's Review of the NIAS Report' noted that NIAS neither examined key project documents nor engaged with stakeholders. In fact, the civil society group used the term 'NIAS-washing' to explain how the unscientific report by NIAS undermined serious ecological concerns raised by members of the statutory body. The review noted that NIAS failed to provide data to support its major claim that Karnataka was resorting to distress sales of power due to a lack of storage facilities. Panel set up by national wildlife board opposes pumped storage project in Sharavathi valley "NIAS does not provide data showing how much surplus electricity was sold through distress sales. This data is critical," it noted, adding that occasional sales could not justify a 2,000 MW PSP. Retired IFS officer and principal chief conservator of forests B K Singh, former Forest Department secretary A N Yellappa Reddy, wildlife biologist Ravi Chellam, ecologist Subash Chandran and others challenged the NIAS report for downplaying Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). They cited the July 2026 report of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, projections by the Central Electricity Authority, and projects taking shape in Gujarat and Karnataka to reject NIAS's reasoning. The review also noted that the report failed to provide the necessary data and evidence to show that the PSP in the Sharavathi Valley would contribute to climate change mitigation. It clarified that the reviewers supported PSP technology and opposed only the project's location in the highly sensitive Sharavathi Valley. Speaking to DH , Singh said the government had evidently tasked NIAS with finding ways and means to make the project acceptable. "The NIAS report, however, has done a shoddy job of it. Members of NBWL and NTCA have recommended the rejection of the PSP, which is portrayed as a clean energy project. The cost of destruction of a mega-diverse forest and creation of another source of disturbance for wildlife can at no stretch be called clean energy," he added. DH sent a detailed set of queries to NIAS but received no response.

articles.title: Ex CJI Chandrachud-led mediation fails, Kapur family trust dispute heads for court battle
articles.summary: New Delhi: Efforts to resolve the bitter dispute over the assets of the R K Family Trust through mediation led by former Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud have failed, paving the way for an adjudication on merits by the Supreme Court . A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran was informed on Thursday that the mediation between Rani Kapur, mother of late industrialist Sunjay Kapur, and her daughter-in-law Priya Kapur had not yielded a settlement. "One can never force a settlement," the bench observed, indicating that the parties would now have to pursue their claims through legal proceedings. Though the court passed no formal order on Thursday, it indicated that the Delhi High Court should decide, within a time-bound framework, the pending application seeking protection and preservation of the trust's assets. Sunjay Kapur Funeral: Karisma Kapoor, Kareena & Saif join family, bid emotional adieu The Supreme Court had, on May 7, referred the dispute to mediation and appointed Chandrachud as mediator with the consent of all parties. With the talks having failed, the apex court will now examine the rival claims on merits. During Thursday's hearing, senior advocate Siddhartha Dave, appearing for Rani Kapur, told the court that his client had sought Rs 6,000 crore to settle her claims but had received no counter-proposal for six months. Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, representing Priya Kapur, said she was unwilling to participate in a joint mediation session with her mother-in-law. Senior advocate Abhimanyu Bhandari, also appearing for Priya, submitted that she was entitled to 60% of the trust's assets, while the remaining 40% was to be divided among Sunjay Kapur's children. The assets were valued at around Rs 30,000 crore by the opposing counsel. Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani, appearing for the children of actor Karisma Kapoor , meanwhile, submitted that they were entitled to a 24-26% share in the trust. The proceedings arose from a plea by Rani Kapur seeking to restrain Priya Kapur and others from interfering with the functioning of the R K Family Trust while the dispute is pending. The family dispute intensified following Sunjay Kapur's death while playing polo in England in June 2025. With mediation now off the table, the competing claims over the substantial family estate will be tested in court.

articles.title: Long Covid: Breathing difficulties persist four years after diagnosis, study reveals
articles.summary: The Covid-19 pandemic is an event of the past; however, its effects have continued to last till now. Around 50 per cent of people reported suffering from breathing difficulties even four years after their initial diagnosis.​ Persistent symptoms of chest tightness, cough, chest pain, headaches, or breathing difficulties after a bout of Covid-19 is called post-covid-19 condition by the World Health Organisation (WHO), or long Covid . It affects people regardless of sex, age, initial disease severity, or prior health status.​ According to the study published in the journal Respiratory Research , dyspnoea, a shortness of breath, is the most common respiratory symptom that people with long Covid experience. Other symptoms like chest tightness, cough, and chest pain are also frequently reported. Researchers at the Karolinska University Hospital in Stockholm, Sweden, analysed data from 288 participants diagnosed with long Covid. They used a 16-question survey called the Nijmegen Questionnaire (NQ) to spot symptoms pointing toward dysfunctional breathing. A score of 23 or higher signalled frequent symptoms of concern.​ Altered breathing patterns are often referred to as dysfunctional breathing, or breathing pattern disorder. It may occur either independently or with an underlying cardiological or neurological condition.​ According to the study findings, people who were not hospitalised when they initially got infected were six times more likely to develop breathing problems four years later, compared to those who were hospitalised. Moreover, being younger, having more shortness of breath early on, or having a slightly lower one-second air-exhale measure (FEV₁) at baseline also made long-term symptoms more likely.​ Apparently, at the first clinic visit, around 11 months after infection, standard breathing tests were fairly similar between groups. However, four years later, those dealing with the long Covid symptoms were walking shorter distances and had weaker inhaling muscle strength. At the four-year mark, 38 per cent of people with high breathing scores also reported a postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), a condition where heart rate jumps sharply upon standing. They also reported having more long Covid symptoms, worse mood/depression scores, and higher rates of being sick.

articles.title: Delimitation | NDA banking on DMK and NCP(SP) for numbers game in Parliament
articles.summary: New Delhi: All eyes are on the DMK and the NCP (Sharad Pawar faction) as the NDA government prepares to convene a brief Parliament session from November 30 to push through the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill linked to the delimitation exercise . The high-stakes legislation seeks to expand the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to around 850 and pave the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies from the 2029 general elections. Constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority. In the present House, that means 361 votes out of 543 to pass the legislation. With three vacancies, at present the effective strength stands at 540. Factoring in the Speaker (who votes only in a tie) and suspended TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee, the government would need roughly 360 votes if 539 members participate. Delimitation bill on cards as Parliament set to reconvene on Nov 30; Centre, Opposition gear up for a stormy session When a similar attempt was made on April 17, the NDA managed only 298 votes and fell short. The numbers have improved since then. The ruling NDA has around 320 members and would need the support of opposition parties to cross the threshold. Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India, extending support to the NDA. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs crossed over to the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. With the Shiromani Akali Dal also returning to the alliance, the NDA’s strength has climbed to approximately 325. To close the remaining gap, the ruling coalition is intensively wooing the DMK’s 22 MPs and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)’s eight. Their support would take the tally to 355 — still five short of the required mark. NDA managers are simultaneously reaching out to smaller parties and independents, including the YSRCP (4), JMM (3), VCK (2) and RLP (1), while hoping for abstentions from some INDIA bloc members. TMC MP Kalyan Benerjee can't attend the House as he was suspended. 'Perhaps it will be good': NCP-SP softening stance on Delimitation Bill? Supriya Sule hints at support In the Rajya Sabha (current strength 242), the NDA has 155 members and needs 162 votes. Backing from the DMK’s eight MPs and the NCP (SP)’s single member would push the number to 164 — two above the threshold. With the session just days away, the political arithmetic remains fluid. The decisions of the DMK and NCP (SP) could prove decisive in what is shaping up to be one of the most closely watched legislative battles of the year.

articles.title: Karnataka government sets up high-level committee to trim Western Ghats ESA
articles.summary: Bengaluru: The State government has set up a high level committee headed by retired judge of Karnataka High Court as well as village-level committees to work on reducing the Eco-Sensitive Area (ESA) of the Western Ghats , a Unesco biodiversity hotspot, proposed by the Centre's notification. The Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) has been issuing draft notifications to declare ESA based on the report submitted by a committee led by former chief of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) K Kasturirangan. The notification entails a set of regulations aimed at restricting harmful projects like mining while supporting eco-friendly activities like agriculture. State seeks ground survey of Western Ghats However, from the first draft notification issued in 2014 to the sixth issued in July this year, the Centre's attempts have been opposed by people's representatives in the ruling party as well as those in the opposition parties. Of the 56,825.7 sq km of total ESA proposed for the entire Western Ghats, Karnataka accounts for 20,668 sq km (36.3%). The State government had in September held a three-day special session of the Legislature to discuss the sixth draft notification. Both the State Assembly and the Council unanimously resolved to urge the Centre to limit the ESA to notified forests, exclude agricultural lands and human habitations, as well as those lands where claims were pending. The nine-member committee chaired by Justice (retd) John Michael D'Cunha will look into the provisions of the Kasturirangan Report and recommend suitable modifications and 'corrective' measures. The committee will take into account ground truthing details and land grants and claims. The notification also constituted gram panchayat-level committees led by the chairman of the panchayat to organise physical verification, create public awareness and receive representations from the public. The four-member committee will finalise the village-level maps and submit it to the high-level panel. Karnataka CM Shivakumar asks Centre for ‘balanced approach’ to coastal, Western Ghats norms 'Misleading the public' Conservationists and civil society organisations have accused the political class of failing to take the people into confidence. Civil society organisations have pointed out that the state government has failed to provide a copy of Kasturirangan report in Kannada, leaving the space for vested interests to mislead the people. For instance, though the notification already excludes agriculture and plantation, fear has been created among many farmers that their livelihood will be affected by restrictions on such activities.

While some were already in the capital following Wednesday’s Cabinet meeting, others had to change schedules at short notice. The Friday meeting will mark a rare instance of the Union Cabinet convening twice in the same week. Several ministers who were scheduled for official foreign trips next week have also cancelled or deferred their programmes to remain present for the parliamentary proceedings.

articles.title: NITES seeks policy framework to protect IT employees from AI-driven job loss
articles.summary: Bengaluru: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES), an IT employees’ union, has called for a comprehensive policy framework to safeguard employees in the Information Technology (IT) and IT-enabled Services (ITeS) sectors from job displacement arising from Artificial Intelligence (AI), automation and other emerging technologies. NITES said it recognises that technological advancement is important to the industry's growth. However, the adoption of AI and automation must not leave employees without adequate notice, financial security or opportunities to transition into alternative employment. NITES has sought mandatory disclosure of AI-related job losses, stating that IT companies must be transparent when undertaking workforce reductions, particularly where such decisions are attributed to AI or automation. Pro-Kannada outfit launches campaign to protect jobs for Kannadigas in IT-BT firms "Employees and government authorities should know how many people are affected, why their positions are being eliminated and how many jobs are directly being replaced by technology," it said. It has also sought mandatory safeguards for affected employees, saying companies adopting AI and automation should be required to provide reasonable advance notice, fair severance compensation and payment of all outstanding statutory and contractual dues. Employers should make genuine efforts to reskill and redeploy existing employees within the organisation before eliminating their positions on account of technological advancements, it said. NITES has called for a dedicated policy-level discussion involving the government, NASSCOM, IT companies and employee representatives to develop a common framework that balances technological innovation and industry growth with employees' rights, dignity and job security. Harpreet Singh Saluja, President of NITES, said companies should be free to adopt new technologies and improve their productivity. However, they must also take responsibility for the employees whose livelihoods are affected by these decisions. “Technological progress cannot become a justification for arbitrary job losses or the denial of employees' rights. We need a framework that ensures transparency, fair compensation, meaningful reskilling and opportunities for redeployment,” he said. NITES urged the government to initiate consultations with industry stakeholders and employee representatives to formulate a forward-looking policy on responsible AI adoption and workforce protection.

articles.summary: New Delhi: Public health campaigners on Thursday said the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) must determine nutrient thresholds in accordance with "robust scientific evidence, established dietary recommendations and international best practices" following the Supreme Court's landmark verdict on food labelling. The apex court ruled that warning thresholds must consider total sugars and saturated fat rather than only added sugars and added fat, alongside salt. "The FSSAI now will have to decide on the level of sugar and salt in food items and regulate them accordingly. The regulator has to determine the thresholds and issue the notification in the next four months. Public health won today as the Supreme Court reminded the State that it is not a bargaining chip," Arun Gupta, a paediatrician who is the convenor of the Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest told DH . Supreme Court orders mandatory red hexagon front-of-package warnings on packaged food; rejects FSSAI’s ‘added sugar’ formula "While the Court has settled for total sugars and saturated fat, separate hexagons for each nutrient of concern, pictorial representation and a minimum 4-5 per cent display area, the real battle now shifts to the thresholds. FSSAI must now choose science based thresholds being used by countries like Chile, Mexico, and the WHO," said Gupta. Earlier this month, the UN health agency came out with a draft plan on how to identify unhealthy food that should be consumed in moderation. The bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said FSSAI would ensure that the front of pack nutritional labelling must consider “total sugars” and “saturated fat”, rather than “added sugar” and “added fat”, as the nutrients-of-concern, alongside “salt”. With the ICMR's National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad listing only "added sugar" in its Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, the apex court asked the food regulator to revisit and reformulate the threshold levels for each nutrient of concern. The bench asserted that the values for sugar and fat provided in the NIN guidelines shall not be adopted since they were calculated with reference to “added sugar” and “added fat”, and not “total sugars” and “saturated fat”. "This can be done if we consider 10 per cent calories from total sugar, 10 per cent calories from saturated fat and one mg sodium per kilo calorie. That should make a good sense to India to define thresholds. This could be discussed among a public health expert group under the leadership of ICMR-NIN," he said. Nutrient thresholds must be guided by robust, independent scientific evidence, established dietary recommendations and international best practices, NAPi said. "The judgement reinforces that protecting people's health is not merely a policy choice; it is an essential part of the State's responsibility to uphold the Right to Life under Article 21 of the Constitution, which encompasses the Right to Health." The Supreme Court advised the FSSAI to fix the thresholds in such a way that they are neither too low nor too high. "Thresholds set too low would result in almost all packaged food products carrying a warning label and thereby desensitise consumers and induce ‘label fatigue’. Thresholds set too high, on the other hand, would allow most products to escape the label altogether, leaving consumers unknowingly exposed to harmful levels of saturated fat, sugar, and salt," the court added. "For years, the food regulator treated 'lack of consensus' as a reason to do nothing. The Supreme Court has now said: consensus is not a prerequisite for public health. The judgement explicitly directs FSSAI not to let industry objections delay regulation and to prioritise public health and consumer interest," Gupta added.

articles.title: Equal access to justice must remain judiciary’s priority, says President Murmu on Constitution Day
articles.summary: New Delhi: President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday stressed the need for timely delivery of justice, quality legal aid for the poor and greater representation of women in the judiciary, saying that equal access to justice was essential to fulfilling the constitutional promise of equality. Addressing the Constitution Day celebrations organised by the Supreme Court of India , the President said the judiciary had made an invaluable contribution to the Republic's journey by upholding the fundamental ideals of justice amid sweeping social and technological changes. She emphasised that timely delivery of justice was an essential component of the very concept of justice. While acknowledging initiatives such as procedural simplification, the use of technology and the establishment of special courts, she flagged the mounting pendency of cases as a major challenge. Supreme Court sends journalists’ police abuse allegations to inquiry panel; flags need to define journalist status "Despite these efforts, the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for our justice delivery system," she said, expressing confidence that concerted efforts at every level would help address the problem. Highlighting the importance of legal aid, Murmu said not everyone had the resources to approach the High Courts or the Supreme Court. The constitutional mandate of equal opportunity, she said, required that no citizen be denied access to justice because of economic constraints or other hardships. She called upon the District, State and National Legal Services Authorities to intensify efforts to ensure that justice reached vulnerable and disadvantaged sections. She also stressed the need to improve the quality and reliability of legal representation available to the poor and marginalised. The President said empathy and ethics deserved as much importance as the study of law in legal education. Urging senior members of the Bar to set inspiring examples, she said young lawyers should see that "excellence can be blended with empathy, and competence with compassion". Calling for greater participation of women in the Bench and Bar, Murmu said a woman's perspective could contribute to inclusion, diversity and balance in judicial decision-making. Greater emphasis on inclusivity and merit, she added, would strengthen the judiciary. India-EU FTA opens new opportunities to deepen trade, technological ties with Bulgaria: Droupadi Murmu She appreciated the Supreme Court's initiatives to prioritise cases involving persons with disabilities, acid attack survivors, senior citizens above 80 years and people below the poverty line. Recalling that the Constitution was adopted on November 26, 1949, she said the annual observance of Constitution Day was instituted in 2015 to mark the 125th birth anniversary of its principal architect, Dr BR Ambedkar. The President said the judiciary must continue to uphold the ideals envisioned by the Constituent Assembly.

articles.title: UN reports shows 47,000 women and girls were killed by a partner or relative in 2025
articles.summary: New Delhi: An estimated 47,000 women and girls were killed by their intimate partners or other family members worldwide in 2025, an average of 129 victims every day, according to a report by UN Women and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC). While the estimate is lower than the 50,000 recorded in 2024, the report cautioned against interpreting the difference as a decline in femicide, saying it largely reflected improvements in the availability of country-level data. Africa recorded the highest estimated number of victims at 22,100, as well as the highest rate of intimate partner and family-member femicide, at 2.9 victims per 100,000 women and girls. The UN agencies, however, said the figures should be interpreted with caution due to gaps in data from some countries in the region. “Globally, an estimated 1.1 women per 100,000 female population were killed by an intimate partner or another family member in 2025,” the report showed. Karnataka to set up dedicated unit to fight online crime against women, children The estimated rate stood at 1.4 per 100,000 women and girls in the Americas, 1.1 in Oceania, 0.6 in Asia and 0.5 in Europe. Of the estimated 78,000 women and girls intentionally killed worldwide in 2025, around 60 per cent were killed by their intimate partners or other family members. Only 11% of male homicide victims were killed by intimate partners or family members, while in the case of women, the number stood at 60%. “The circumstances under which intimate partner violence escalates into lethal violence have been widely analysed by criminologists and other researchers.A set of risk factors has been identified, including a history of violence between the perpetrator and the victim, previous threats and an actual or imminent separation.Some findings also suggest that being a foreign woman in a given country with no or limited social support, could increase the probability being killed,” the report stated. Who’s at the peace table? Why the UN’s Women, Peace and Security agenda is failing Over 2010–2025, the rate of femicide committed by intimate partners or family members in Europe declined gradually, by nearly a third. The report also highlighted the slow pace of decline in intimate partner and family-member femicide. Between 2010 and 2025, the rate fell from 1.6 to 1.4 per 100,000 women and girls in the Americas, a decline of 12%. In Europe, it dropped from 0.7 to 0.5, a reduction of 28%. The findings underline the need for domestic violence prevention measures to address violence not only within intimate relationships but also across wider family structures, where women and girls remain vulnerable to lethal violence.

articles.title: Indian students, workers top exit tally as UK logs net migration fall
articles.summary: London: Indian students and workers topped the tally of visa-holders leaving the UK as the country’s latest net migration data released on Thursday repeated a downward trend from previous figures. The UK’s Office for National Statistics (ONS) data reveals that 55,000 Indians on study visas and 28,000 on work visas had emigrated from the country in the year ending June 2026. An additional 2,000 Indian nationals logged under the “other” visa category also exited the country in that period, making up a total of 85,000 Indian emigrants followed by 51,000 Chinese nationals as the second highest in the UK's exit tally. “Among people emigrating, Indian was the most common non-EU+ nationality,” the ONS stated. Pakistani, Bangladeshi migrants pretend to be gay to claim asylum in UK: Report The agency found that net migration, the difference between people immigrating to and emigrating from the UK, fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026. A trend was logged in November 2025 and is being led by nationals from countries outside the European Union (EU), such as India, China, Nigeria and Pakistan . Indians, meanwhile, also continue to be reflected in the top tally for immigration into the UK, with 77,000 logged under study visa grants and 40,000 for work purposes. Alongside the ONS data covering migration, the UK Home Office has also released data covering illegal migration and asylum claims for the year to September 2026. It shows that 31,000 people were detected arriving in the UK illegally, with people arriving via small boats across the English Channel accounting for 86 per cent of them. "This government has restored control," said UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. "We have brought net migration to 77,000, down 92 per cent from its peak under the previous government. Where they failed, we have delivered for the British people. "This didn’t happen by accident. It happened because this government took action. But we won't stop here,” she said. Reducing net migration has been among the British government’s priorities due to pressures of soaring immigration figures on the economy in recent years. The latest ONS data shows that immigration fell by 155,000 over the year to June -- from 893,000 to 738,000 -- while emigration fell by 28,000 from 689,000 to 661,000.
